newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Howard defends official's shares.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Howard defends official's shares.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard on Monday said a senior government official's ownership of banking shares did not breach his administration's ethics guidelines.

Howard has come under fire from the Labor opposition over share ownership by ministers and senior officials, including the parliamentary secretary to the treasurer, Brian Gibson, who sold off bank shares in recent days.
"Because he was not assigned specific responsibility for banking legislation, I did not believe that he was in breach of the guidelines," Howard told parliament.
"For more abundant caution, he has sold those shares, but I do not concede that in relation to the allegation that you have made he was in breach of the guidelines," Howard said.
Assistant Treasurer Jim Short resigned on Saturday after breaching Howard's ethics rules by retaining banking shares while in charge of banking matters.
Howard published the ethics guidelines soon after his March 2 election win as part of a declared campaign to raise ministerial standards of accountability.
